entries.claim: The inspected CC Switch implementation discovers supported CLIs through the PATH-default command plus audited fallback directories, executes bounded --version probes, distinguishes not-found from installed-but-broken, and has separate Windows command-script and App Execution Alias handling.

The locally installed official @deepseek-ai/dsh package is version 0.1.0-rc.6, points to github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, and documents dsh web as the web-profile alias, but its public CLI documentation does not establish a stable user-owned Base URL field or a safe automatic-write adapter contract.

The first governed RU-003 verification run executed five scenarios successfully but the catalog scenario failed because invoking Vitest inside the mandatory read-only source sandbox attempted to create vitest.config.ts.timestamp-*.mjs in the project root. After replacing that nested runner with direct Node TypeScript module execution, local execution passed all six scenarios; redispatch was then blocked because the dispatcher revalidated the completed RU-002 dependency against RU-003's intentionally superseding current UI outputs.

At commit 72644de the desktop shell has truthful account and billing unavailable states, a five-tool read-only local scan, and a five-tool two-line configuration preview, but it has no home guidance destination, no line-connectivity query, no settings and security destination, bundle output is disabled, updater artifacts are disabled, and the Tauri runtime exposes only scan_tools_read_only.

Run 33335919230 at commit 548d897 compiled Windows tests with native temp, then failed with c1010070 and LNK1327 when cargo re-linked under a WSL UNC TEMP. The inherited workflows also name an unregistered config atomic-write test and cc_switch_lib, while ci.yml only triggers main and the active crate is yeschoy_desktop_lib with six pure tests.

On 2026-08-29, the latest published stable GitHub releases were Claude Code v2.1.251, Codex rust-v0.151.0, OpenCode v1.18.25, and Pi v0.84.4. The DSH repository had no GitHub Release and its newest tag was dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1, so these versions are current research anchors rather than a verified 野菜API support matrix.

Exact-tag source inspection found the required extension seams in the current research anchors: Claude Code v2.1.251 includes recent apiKeyHelper-only gateway fixes; Codex rust-v0.146.0 through rust-v0.151.0 each include command-backed provider bearer-token schema and tests; OpenCode v1.18.25 exposes the authentication loader hook; Pi v0.84.4 documents request-time !command apiKey resolution; and DSH dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1 exposes a credential-provider seam but explicitly ships no keyring or helper-command provider. This verifies source structure, not cross-platform 野菜API compatibility.

The current official Codex configuration reference documents ~/.codex/config.toml, model_providers.<id>.base_url, responses-only wire_api, and model_providers.<id>.auth.command as a command that prints a bearer token to stdout; auth.command must not be combined with env_key, experimental_bearer_token, or requires_openai_auth.

The current official Claude Code documentation identifies ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL as the custom endpoint setting and apiKeyHelper as a dynamic script-based credential source, supporting a preview of owned settings without placing a literal API key in settings.

The current official OpenCode provider documentation defines custom providers under provider.<id>, uses @ai-sdk/openai-compatible for OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoints, accepts options.baseURL, and identifies model entries by their exact model IDs.

The current official Pi models documentation identifies ~/.pi/agent/models.json, provider baseUrl and api fields, exact model IDs, OpenAI-compatible API modes, and an apiKey value beginning with ! as a command evaluated at request time.

Current official Tauri v2 distribution guidance supports platform-specific installers and states that direct macOS distribution requires code signing and notarization while Windows distribution provides installer and code-signing paths.
Current Apple guidance requires appropriate Developer ID signing, hardened runtime, secure timestamping, notarization review, and testing for directly distributed macOS software.

Current Microsoft guidance states that unsigned downloads can show SmartScreen warnings, may be blocked by enterprise policy or Smart App Control, and do not carry publisher reputation between versions.

Current Tauri v2 updater guidance requires signed update artifacts, keeps the verification public key in the client, and requires the signing private key only in the protected build environment; update signature verification cannot be disabled.
GitHub currently provides windows-2025 x64, macos-15-intel Intel, and macos-15 arm64 hosted runners for private repositories; hosted runs consume the account's Actions allowance.
GitHub workflows with workflow_call can be called by another workflow through a local ./.github/workflows/file.yml reference at the caller's commit without inheriting secrets.

V1 should configure only exact tool versions that passed the complete Windows and macOS adapter matrix, with the signed client carrying the allowlist. The first verification cohort should use the three latest stable releases at test-baseline time for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi, while DSH is evaluated separately against one exact prerelease tag. Unknown, newly released, and failed versions remain read-only and never receive a plaintext compatibility fallback.

entries.claim: RU-003 should add a deterministic beginner configuration-preview planner for the fixed five-tool catalog and the two product-approved line roots. It may show only evidenced target fields and derived protocol endpoints, must leave the model ID unavailable until a server catalog exists, and must block all configuration, credential, file-read, file-write, connectivity, and rollback actions until later backend, secure-helper, and exact-version evidence is frozen.

A verification-only successor release unit should preserve RU-003 product behavior and source exactly, use the corrected direct-module acceptance scenario under the mandatory read-only sandbox, retain the original failed run as historical evidence, and avoid replaying the dispatcher dependency check that compares intentionally superseded UI outputs to RU-002.

RU-005 should supersede RU-004 and finish the bounded client-side V1 candidate by adding a guided home, user-triggered secret-free DNS and TCP-443 diagnostics for only the two approved line hosts, a settings and security truth surface, complete multilingual page states, candidate bundle configuration, and platform and backend handoff checklists while login, models, prices, credentials, configuration writes, retained backups, telemetry upload, signed updates, and production release remain unavailable.
V1 serves novice users who already installed their AI tools but do not know how to configure them; tool installation is deferred.
V1 supports Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH (DeepSeek Harness).
The mainland-optimized and Cloudflare global-acceleration lines share the same account, API key, model availability, and pricing semantics; only the network path differs.

The default model list shows models available to the current account and compatible with the selected tool; all models may be viewed with unavailable entries disabled and explained, and a removed model is never silently substituted.

The product owner confirmed the Claude Code and Codex credential-helper rule: their per-tool relay keys stay in the operating-system credential vault, unsupported versions must prompt for upgrade, and the client must never fall back to plaintext key storage for compatibility.

The product owner confirmed that DSH V1 formally supports one-click configuration only for the web profile; headless, sdk, sdk-minimal, acp, and other profiles are read-only discovery targets and must not be modified in V1.

The product owner confirmed the V1 secure credential integration for the remaining tools: OpenCode uses a signed authentication plugin whose runtime loader calls the credential helper, Pi uses its native command-backed apiKey contract, and DSH uses a version-pinned operating-system-vault credential provider. Missing or incompatible security components must block configuration with no plaintext fallback.

The product owner accepted the exact-version compatibility allowlist for V1: automatic configuration is enabled only for exact tool versions that passed the complete matrix, while unknown, newly released, failed, and otherwise unverified versions remain read-only until a trusted compatibility update adds them.

The product owner rejected presenting DSH as a Developer Preview and stated that the current DSH version is materially settled. DSH web is therefore a normal V1 support target after exact-version verification, without a product preview badge; this product decision does not convert the upstream prerelease tag into an official stable release or prove compatibility before testing.

The product owner confirmed that incomplete DSH web compatibility must not block the overall V1 release. If no exact DSH version has passed the mandatory matrix at release time, DSH remains discovery-only with no configuration or credential writes until a later trusted client update adds verified support.

The product owner authorized development to begin with a governed first release unit limited to the 野菜API desktop shell, product branding, and read-only discovery and compatibility reporting for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH; account login, billing, recharge, NewAPI changes, secrets, configuration writes, automatic updates, and telemetry are excluded from this unit.

The product owner authorized implementation to continue after RU-002 and accepted starting the next client-only one-click configuration foundation while preserving the decision not to modify NewAPI, servers, Nginx, DNS, databases, or production configuration in this phase.

The product owner authorized one continuous goal to finish the client-side 野菜API V1 candidate without incremental approval pauses, while preserving the existing prohibition on changing NewAPI, servers, Nginx, DNS, databases, or production and without fabricating backend-dependent success.

After diagnosing the inherited WSL2 Nightly failure, the product owner authorized adapting the client CI, pushing the correction, and verifying Windows and macOS results without modifying NewAPI or publishing installers.

decisions.question: How should the accepted RU-003 implementation be verified after the original frozen acceptance runner proved incompatible with mandatory read-only isolation and redispatch rechecked superseded dependency outputs?
decisions.choice: Create RU-004 as a verification-only successor to RU-003. Preserve the RU-003 product scope, source, contract, page, and blocked side-effect boundary without modification; execute the same six semantic scenarios using the corrected direct Node TypeScript module loader plus read-only source assertions; retain the original failed run as immutable historical evidence; and declare no work-package dependency because RU-004 changes no implementation and its release-unit dependency and supersession preserve the authority chain.

decisions.question: How should inherited upstream CI be adapted without expanding candidate runtime or release authority?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-006 as a CI-only unit depending on the completed RU-005 candidate. Replace main-only upstream checks with current candidate checks on main and product/** push and PR plus manual invocation; retain nightly scheduling by reusing the same workflow at the same commit. Run frontend type checking, current candidate tests and acceptance, Rust formatting/Clippy, and nonempty native test execution on Windows x64 and both macOS architectures. Keep native temp directories; fail for missing/current test identities, empty/ignored/filtered suites, compile and test failures. Do not compile the inactive CC Switch config module merely to preserve an irrelevant WSL write test. Explicitly state that this unit does not validate WSL configuration writes, signing, installers, runtime GUI, or production. No release, deployment, secret, repository-permission, NewAPI or product behavior change.

requirements.statement: V1 detects installed instances of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH and reports installed, not found, configured, needs attention, and unsupported-version states.
acceptance: Every supported tool has an explicit detection contract and version evidence.
Not found is not presented as an error.
An unsupported or ambiguous installation is not modified.

requirements.statement: V1 does not download, install, update, or uninstall third-party AI tools.
acceptance: A missing tool receives installation guidance only.
No V1 action elevates privileges to install a third-party tool.

requirements.statement: V1 automatically configures a third-party tool only when that exact tool version is present in the signed compatibility allowlist backed by complete platform, credential, configuration, request, conflict, recovery, removal, and secret-leak evidence.
acceptance: Every allowlisted version names its exact upstream tag or package version, adapter-contract version, supported platform cells, evidence set, and client catalog version.
A minimum-version comparison, an open semantic-version range, source-level feature presence, or a successful test on only one platform cannot independently grant automatic-configuration support.

A newly released, unknown, prerelease, failed, unparsable, or multiply installed version stays read-only and cannot create credentials, write configuration, install plugins, or alter defaults unless its exact identity is explicitly allowlisted.

Each allowlisted platform cell passes detection, configuration preview, credential delivery, atomic write and read-back, real tool-level request, override and conflict handling, interrupted-transaction recovery, receipt-matching removal, and complete-secret scanning.
Compatibility allowlist changes ship only inside a signed client or signed compatibility artifact governed by the updater trust boundary, and a stale or unverifiable catalog fails closed.

An exact DSH upstream prerelease tag may be allowlisted only after the full matrix passes; when it passes, it is presented as normal V1 support without a product preview badge while its exact upstream version remains visible, and it does not imply support for another DSH tag or profile.

requirements.statement: Incomplete DSH web compatibility does not block the overall V1 release; until an exact DSH version completes every mandatory gate, DSH remains discovery-only with no configuration or credential writes and may gain normal support only through a later trusted signed client update.
acceptance: The overall V1 release-readiness result is not failed solely because no exact DSH web version has yet completed every required platform and security cell.

An unverified DSH installation is visibly reported as detected but not currently supported for automatic configuration and exposes no configure, repair, remove, line-switch, model-write, plugin-install, or credential action.
Allowing the overall release never relaxes the exact-version allowlist, credential-vault, no-plaintext-fallback, web-profile-only, or truthful-support-display boundaries.
A later signed client update may add normal DSH support only after an exact version passes the complete matrix; discovery-only status does not silently convert into support.
Release notes, product pages, and in-app supported-tool lists state the actually verified tool set and do not claim DSH automatic configuration before evidence exists.

requirements.statement: RU-001 provides a beginner-readable 野菜API desktop shell that performs only local read-only discovery of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH and reports exact detected versions and conservative compatibility truth without contacting a server or changing the machine.
acceptance: The primary screen names 野菜API and explains in plain language that it is checking already-installed tools without asking for an API key, Base URL, model name, or configuration-file path.

One explicit scan returns exactly one result for each of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH and distinguishes not found, detected but unverified, executable failure or timeout, and ambiguous multiple-installation states.

Every detected version string remains visible; a version not present in a later verified exact-version allowlist is reported as read-only and exposes no configure, repair, remove, install, line, model, credential, login, billing, recharge, updater, or telemetry action.
The scan performs no HTTP or other network request, does not read tool configuration contents, does not access a credential store, and creates, modifies, or deletes no user or tool file.
A failed or timed-out probe affects only that tool card, keeps the other tool results visible, provides a safe rescan action, and never guesses installation or compatibility.
Repeated scans replace stale results by request identity so an older completion cannot overwrite the newest visible scan.

requirements.statement: RU-003 preserves RU-002 and adds a beginner-readable local configuration preview for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH across the mainland-optimized and global-accelerated lines without reading or changing any tool configuration, accessing a credential, contacting a server, or inventing a model ID.
acceptance: The configuration destination presents exactly Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH in stable order and lets the user choose exactly one tool for the current preview.
The line step presents exactly mainland optimized at https://yeschoy.com and global accelerated at https://api.yeschoy.com, and the selected line root remains visible in the summary.

Claude Code previews the approved root URL, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi preview the selected root with /v1, and DSH explicitly withholds a protocol endpoint and write target because its exact web-profile adapter is not verified.
The preview names only evidenced user-owned fields, exposes no literal secret or complete user path, and clearly states that it has not read an existing configuration.
Model ID remains visibly unavailable pending the first-party model catalog; the UI displays no sample model, guessed model, price, connectivity result, or supported-version claim.
The apply control remains disabled and the projection reports networkAttempted, configurationRead, configurationWritten, and credentialAccessed as false for every tool and line selection.
RU-001 local discovery and RU-002 account and billing readiness behavior remain available and unchanged, and no NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, updater, or production resource is modified.

requirements.statement: RU-005 preserves all prior truthful client boundaries and completes a cohesive client-side V1 candidate with beginner guidance, bounded two-line connectivity evidence, settings and security truth, complete multilingual states, candidate bundle preparation, and an actionable future NewAPI handoff without claiming production or backend readiness.
acceptance: The default destination gives a beginner one ordered path through local tool discovery, line choice and preview, account integration truth, and diagnostics, with no API, Base URL, configuration-file, or secret knowledge required.

The account and billing destination still displays no fabricated login, balance, usage, model ID, official price, actual price, or recharge result, and configuration apply remains disabled for every tool and line.

Connectivity runs only after an explicit user action, checks exactly yeschoy.com:443 and api.yeschoy.com:443 through a closed local query, returns only bounded DNS and TCP outcomes with latency and correlation, sends no HTTP or model request, and never accesses or uploads a credential, cookie, prompt, response, configuration, complete local path, or raw network error.

The diagnostic UI distinguishes default, processing, partial success, complete failure, stale result, invalid projection, and recovery, and explicitly says TCP reachability does not prove API, account, model, or billing health.

Settings makes language selection, no-retained-backup policy, secret boundary, inactive telemetry upload, inactive updater, candidate version, and release gates visible without exposing an action that exceeds current authority.

A candidate-only Tauri bundle overlay exists for local Windows and macOS packaging while automatic updater artifacts remain disabled; the release checklist requires native-platform builds, macOS Developer ID signing and notarization for direct public distribution, and an explicit unsigned-Windows beta warning until a real signing path exists.
All four supported languages contain the candidate navigation and page copy, the UI remains usable at 320 CSS pixels, and keyboard focus remains visible.

The future NewAPI handoff names the exact interfaces needed for authorization, bootstrap, account, usage, models, server-projected official-versus-actual prices, tool keys, telemetry, compatibility catalog, and update separation while recording that none is deployed or modified by RU-005.

requirements.statement: The current candidate branch and nightly schedule execute the same bounded read-only-source CI checks with explicit Windows x64 and macOS Intel/Apple Silicon native results, rejecting empty/stale/skipped test suites without pretending to validate legacy WSL configuration writes or public release.
acceptance: Push and PR to main and product/** trigger candidate checks without path filters silently omitting current changes; manual runs and nightly reuse run the same workflow definition.
Frontend checks execute the existing test:candidate script and RU-005 acceptance, not superseded upstream or historical acceptance suites; package installation is frozen-lockfile.

Windows x64, macOS Intel and Apple Silicon run Rust formatting, Clippy and current library tests using native temporary directories and current crate identity; no WSL path or old atomic-write selector remains.
A test runner fails for compile errors, missing or ambiguous test artifacts, stale identity, zero tests, missing required candidate cases, test failures, ignored/filtered cases and timeouts.
Workflows use read-only contents permissions, pinned action SHAs, no persisted checkout credentials, no inherited secrets, no release/deployment commands and isolated native caches.
Local semantic tests do not substitute for actual hosted results; the CI guide identifies the old incident, current scopes, native test proof, nightly recovery and release/WSL limitations.

invariants: V1 observes but does not install, update, or uninstall third-party AI tools.
A diagnostic conclusion names only causes supported by collected evidence.
A configuration write cannot commit without an encrypted transaction-scoped rollback snapshot and external-change check; no successful transaction retains backup history.

contracts.authorization: Callable only by the bundled local desktop webview after an explicit user action. It may resolve and open TCP port 443 only for the two compiled first-party hosts and grants no HTTP, model, account, credential, configuration, filesystem-write, telemetry, updater, DNS-change, or server-management authority.
contracts.idempotency: The query is read-only and creates no retained record. Repeating it produces a new point-in-time observation; the UI accepts only the newest requestId.
contracts.compatibility: Version 1 always checks exactly two compiled line hosts and returns the closed outcome vocabulary. Adding a host, protocol request, payload, redirect, secret, repair action, or outcome requires a new contract version and accepted decision.

requestId.description: Caller-generated correlation identifier used to reject stale UI results.

outputSchema.description: Point-in-time DNS and TCP-443 evidence for both approved 野菜API line hosts.

startedAtEpochMs.description: Local start timestamp in Unix milliseconds.

completedAtEpochMs.description: Local completion timestamp in Unix milliseconds.

lines.description: Exactly one observation for each approved line in stable product order.

displayName.description: Compiled beginner-readable Chinese line name; localized display is owned by the client.

rootUrl.description: Compiled HTTPS root shown for identification only; no HTTP request is made.

host.description: Compiled first-party hostname used for the bounded resolver and socket operation.

port.description: The only permitted TCP destination port.

status.description: Bounded DNS and TCP outcome with no API-health inference.

latencyMs.description: Elapsed local wall-clock milliseconds for this bounded observation; it is not a model-response speed claim.

reasonCode.description: Stable safe presentation reason that contains no raw resolver or socket error.

observability.correlation: The requestId is returned unchanged and may be shown locally in advanced details.
observability.audit: RU-005 creates no retained diagnostic record and uploads no event.
observability.metrics: Latency and outcome exist only in the current in-memory page state; no metric, hostname result, address, or error text is uploaded or persisted.

errorSemantics: An invalid requestId rejects the whole query before any DNS or TCP operation.
The implementation uses only the two compiled host and port pairs and accepts no caller-provided URL, host, port, path, header, body, credential, proxy, or redirect.
DNS resolution failure, TCP connection failure, and timeout remain distinct safe reason codes; raw resolver and socket errors and resolved addresses are never returned.
A reachable result proves only that a TCP connection to port 443 completed at that moment and must not be presented as proof of TLS, HTTP, API, account, model, price, billing, or inference health.
One line failure does not suppress the other line result, and a stale request completion cannot replace the newest visible result.

contracts.authorization: Callable only by the bundled local desktop webview; it grants no account, credential, filesystem-write, installation, update, or network authority.
contracts.idempotency: The query is read-only. Repeating one request against the same executable paths yields an equivalent projection; the UI accepts results only for its newest requestId.
contracts.compatibility: Version 1 always returns the fixed five-tool catalog and the declared conservative statuses. New fields or status meanings require a new contract version.

requestId.description: Caller-generated correlation identifier used to reject stale UI results.

outputSchema.description: The complete bounded projection for the five V1 tools.

platform.description: The platform family on which discovery ran.

startedAtEpochMs.description: Local monotonic correlation timestamp expressed as Unix milliseconds for freshness display.

completedAtEpochMs.description: Completion timestamp expressed as Unix milliseconds and never earlier than startedAtEpochMs.

tools.description: Exactly one result for every V1 tool in stable product order.

status.description: Observed installation and executable outcome without inferred configuration health.

version.description: Exact normalized version output when available, otherwise an empty string.

candidateCount.description: Number of distinct executable candidates found after canonical-path deduplication.

locationHint.description: A sanitized source hint such as PATH or common location, never a complete user path or OS username.

compatibility.description: Conservative automatic-configuration eligibility for this release unit.

reasonCode.description: Stable presentation reason with no raw command output or secret-bearing diagnostic text.

observability.correlation: requestId is returned unchanged and shown in advanced local details only.
observability.audit: RU-001 emits no persistent audit record; the current in-memory result is the sole local projection.
observability.metrics: RU-001 sends no telemetry and records no persistent metrics; elapsed time is computed in memory for the current scan only.

errorSemantics: An invalid requestId rejects the whole query before any probe starts.
A missing executable is a successful not_found result rather than a command failure.
A non-zero or empty version command becomes probe_failed for only that tool and raw stdout or stderr is not returned.
A probe exceeding the bounded timeout is killed and becomes probe_timed_out for only that tool.
More than one canonical executable becomes multiple_installations and no candidate is silently selected as compatible.
Any detected version not backed by a verified exact-version allowlist is unverified_read_only.

default.behavior: Show the fixed five-tool selector, two approved line choices, unavailable model step, and a deterministic preview summary for the current default selection.
default.visibleTruth: The page is planning only; it has not read configuration, contacted a server, accessed a credential, or established automatic-configuration support.
prohibitedClaims: Do not call the preview configured, connected, compatible, tested, or ready to apply.
default.freshness: The projection is compiled into RU-003 and has no remote freshness timestamp.
default.recovery: The user may change the selection or leave without changing the machine.
default.correlation: Each selection creates a transient requestId for the pure local projection.

loading.behavior: Reserve a bounded placeholder for a future model-catalog request while keeping apply disabled and all remote facts hidden.
loading.visibleTruth: RU-003 does not enter this state because it performs no network request.
prohibitedClaims: Do not retain a previous model or price as current while a future request is unresolved.
loading.freshness: A future newest requestId would own this state.
loading.recovery: A future failure returns to an unavailable model state without guessing.
loading.correlation: The reserved state belongs to exactly one future requestId.

empty.behavior: Keep the selected tool and line visible while explaining that no server model catalog is available.
empty.visibleTruth: No real model ID, price, or model recommendation was obtained.
prohibitedClaims: Do not render a sample or default model as a real account option.
empty.recovery: A later frozen server integration may replace the empty model step.
empty.correlation: The local selection requestId remains transient.

partial.behavior: Show the evidenced tool target fields and selected line root while withholding any endpoint or target that is not established, including DSH.
partial.visibleTruth: Only the named documented preview fields are available; model, credential, support, write, and connectivity facts are absent.
prohibitedClaims: Do not fill an unverified field from another tool adapter.
partial.freshness: The preview catalog is fixed to RU-003 evidence.
partial.recovery: Choose another tool or wait for a later verified adapter release.
partial.correlation: The partial preview belongs to the newest local selection requestId.

error.behavior: Reject an invalid local selection and show no preview or apply action.
error.visibleTruth: The pure projection did not accept the tool, line, or request identity.
prohibitedClaims: Do not fall back to an arbitrary tool, line, model, endpoint, or file.
error.recovery: Reset to the fixed first tool and first line without any side effect.
error.correlation: The safe local error is associated only with the rejected requestId.

expired.behavior: Discard a superseded selection result before it can replace the newest visible preview.
expired.visibleTruth: An older local projection no longer owns the selected tool or line.
prohibitedClaims: Do not merge the endpoint, file, or fields of different selections.
expired.freshness: Only the newest selection requestId is current.
expired.recovery: Continue with the newest projection; no file recovery is required.
expired.correlation: Expired identities remain transient and are not logged.

conflict.behavior: Keep apply disabled when tool identity, exact version, profile, target ownership, or external-change safety cannot be proved.
conflict.visibleTruth: The required future write preconditions are not satisfied.
prohibitedClaims: Do not silently choose an executable, profile, configuration owner, or merge result.
conflict.freshness: A conflict cannot be cleared by the static preview catalog.
conflict.recovery: A later exact-version adapter and transactional read-back flow must resolve it.
conflict.correlation: No secret-bearing or complete local path is included in conflict details.

recovery.behavior: Explain the missing backend, model catalog, secure credential helper, exact-version allowlist, and DSH adapter prerequisites by name.
recovery.visibleTruth: No rollback exists because RU-003 never begins a write transaction.
prohibitedClaims: Do not offer backup restore, repair, credential entry, or force apply in this release unit.
recovery.freshness: Recovery guidance is fixed to the RU-003 release boundary.
recovery.recovery: Wait for a later frozen integration or inspect the local tool discovery result.
recovery.correlation: No persistent operation or recovery identity is created.

processing.behavior: Reserve the future transaction state for encrypted temporary snapshot, guarded write, read-back, tool probe, and rollback while exposing none of those operations in RU-003.
processing.visibleTruth: No configuration operation is processing in RU-003.
prohibitedClaims: Do not animate or label the disabled apply control as if a write, test, or rollback has started.
processing.recovery: No transaction recovery is required because no transaction can start.

pages.purpose: Guide a beginner through tool and line selection and show a truthful configuration preview while every side-effecting operation remains blocked.
permissions: pure local deterministic preview projection only

packages.objective: The current candidate branch and nightly schedule execute the same bounded read-only-source CI checks with explicit Windows x64 and macOS Intel/Apple Silicon native results, rejecting empty/stale/skipped test suites without pretending to validate legacy WSL configuration writes or public release.
deliverables: Push and PR to main and product/** trigger candidate checks without path filters silently omitting current changes; manual runs and nightly reuse run the same workflow definition.
Frontend checks execute the existing test:candidate script and RU-005 acceptance, not superseded upstream or historical acceptance suites; package installation is frozen-lockfile.

Windows x64, macOS Intel and Apple Silicon run Rust formatting, Clippy and current library tests using native temporary directories and current crate identity; no WSL path or old atomic-write selector remains.
A test runner fails for compile errors, missing or ambiguous test artifacts, stale identity, zero tests, missing required candidate cases, test failures, ignored/filtered cases and timeouts.
Workflows use read-only contents permissions, pinned action SHAs, no persisted checkout credentials, no inherited secrets, no release/deployment commands and isolated native caches.
Local semantic tests do not substitute for actual hosted results; the CI guide identifies the old incident, current scopes, native test proof, nightly recovery and release/WSL limitations.
nonGoals: No product runtime, UI, tool configuration, credential, NewAPI, server, deployment, release, signing or updater changes.
No restored upstream config module or claim of WSL write compatibility; no skipped-failure green CI.
No alteration of inherited release or repository-management workflows beyond the two CI entrypoints.

migrationPolicy.dataBackfill: Only repository CI definitions and validation helpers change; no user or server data is touched.
migrationPolicy.rollback: Revert the two CI definitions and owned CI helpers through Git; preserve run history and do not change secrets or production.

compatibilityPolicy.strategy: CI consumes the unchanged RU-005 source and tests; scheduled and push workflows share one definition and current library identity.
compatibilityPolicy.supportedVersions: Current candidate commit on windows-2025 x64, macos-15-intel x64 and macos-15 arm64 runners; no installer or WSL write compatibility claim.
compatibilityPolicy.removalGate: Runtime, credentials, WSL configuration writes, signing, deployments or release authorization require a separate accepted frozen unit.

requiredAcceptanceScenarios.assertion: Main and product branches, manual invocation, and the preserved nightly schedule all bind to the same current CI.
The frontend uses the current candidate commands and all three native platform jobs run lint and nonempty current library tests.
Only read-only contents, pinned actions and non-persisted checkout credentials exist; no WSL overrides, publish commands or masked failures.
The native runner uses cargo machine artifacts for yeschoy_desktop_lib and verifies a complete successful run.
Missing, old, duplicate, or zero-test artifacts fail closed before a success can be claimed.
Compile, execution, ignored/filtered test counts, incomplete summaries, missing baseline cases and timeout failures cannot produce a green result.
The CI guide explains clean reruns and concurrency cancellation without claiming WSL write or release readiness.

stopConditions: Any source modification is needed outside the CI-only owned paths.
GitHub operation would require publishing, external credentials, a permissions change or modifying NewAPI/production.
Current native test failures require changes to frozen product behavior; report evidence and create a successor authority instead of masking them.
